newsitem.title: CANADA: Nebraska firms to build Canada gas additive plant.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska firms to build Canada gas additive plant.

text.p: A consortium of Omaha, Nebraska-based companies including CalEnergy Co Inc, ConAgra Inc and Peter Kiewit Sons Inc announced plans on Wednesday to build a US$450 million gasoline additive plant in Edmonton, Alberta.

The Alberta BioClean renewable ethers facility is slated to begin converting barley and butane into ETBE and MTBE, mostly for the California market, by 1999. Construction will start in the spring of 1997, the firms said.
The gasoline additives are used to reduce automobile emissions.
The plant is expected to take in 650,000 metric tons of grain and 250 million gallons of butane per year, the companies said.
BioClean president and chief executive David Hallberg said at a ceremony on Wednesday that up to 75 percent of the plant's output would likely be sold to California.
Hallberg said the plant would use Alberta's existing pipeline system, which has extensive links to California, to ship its product.
